keyAndScale.keySignature: Three flats (Bb, Eb, Ab) for C natural minor, with B natural accidentals over the dominant G7
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: C minor is the relative minor of Eb major

mainProgression.description: The classic Andalusian cadence in C minor, reimagined through 1950s jump blues and swing. Brian Setzer dresses up the chords with sophisticated jazz voicings (Cm6, Bb9, Abmaj7, and G7#9), creating an irresistible feline swagger.

sectionProgressions.description: Chromatic bass walks connecting tight, syncopated jazz-chord stabs that emulate a stealthy cat prowling through an alley
Hypnotic descending progression driven by Lee Rocker's slapping upright bass and Setzer's half-step chord slides
Rhythm intensifies with driving backbeat snaps and singing group vocal unisons
A classic jazz minor ii-V-i turnaround that shifts the tonal center to the subdominant minor (Fm) before resolving through a half-diminished chord

sectionProgressions.progression: Cm - Bb - Ab - G7 - Fm - Cm - Dm7b5 - G7
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: i - bVII - bVI - V7 - iv - i - iiø7 - V7
sectionProgressions.description: Brian Setzer's masterclass in rockabilly guitar: combining blues grit, swing arpeggios, chromatic enclosures, and Bigsby vibrato dips

harmonicFunction: Cm (i) - Dark tonic minor establishing the cool, nocturnal alleyway atmosphere
Bb (bVII) - Subtonic chord providing effortless descending voice leading
Ab (bVI) - Submediant chord adding poignant weight to the downward motion
G7 (V7) - Major dominant chord containing the leading tone (B natural) that pulls urgently back to Cm
Dm7b5 (iiø7) - Half-diminished chord in the bridge creating authentic jazz-noir tension before the G7 turnaround

techniques.name: Thumb-Pick Hybrid Rockabilly Slap
techniques.description: Brian Setzer's thumb-pick and bare-finger technique. Plucking alternating bass notes with a plastic thumb pick while popping and plucking chord stabs with fingers 1, 2, and 3, creating simultaneous bass, rhythm, and melody

notes: Wear a snug plastic thumb pick on the right-hand thumb for biting, articulate bass notes
Use the flesh and nail of the index, middle, and ring fingers to pluck upper chord tones
Execute sharp fret-hand releases to achieve crisp, staccato chording
Incorporate slap-mutes where the pick-hand heel slaps the strings on beats 2 and 4
sequence: Strike the root note on string 5 with the thumb pick
Pluck strings 4, 3, and 2 simultaneously with fingers 1, 2, and 3
Release fret-hand pressure immediately to stop the chord from ringing
Slide into subsequent chords from one half-step below for authentic jump-blues flair
tips: If you do not use a thumb pick, use a standard flatpick held between thumb and index, using fingers 2 and 3 for hybrid picking
Practice the chromatic bass walk-ins between chord shapes slowly at 90 BPM
Keep the rhythm strictly swinging with dotted-eighth and sixteenth subdivisions

techniques.name: Jazz-Rockabilly Chromatic Enclosures & Bigsby Dips
techniques.description: Approaching chord tones from a half-step above and below before resolving, combined with subtle, expressive dips of the Bigsby vibrato arm on sustained double stops and chords

notes: Target chord tones (roots, 3rds, 5ths) by framing them with chromatic passing notes
Rest the palm over the Bigsby vibrato arm while picking
Apply gentle downward dips of a half-step on final chord ringouts
Blend minor pentatonic blues licks with diminished 7th arpeggio sweeps over the G7 chord
sequence: Play fret 4 on string 3, fret 6, then resolve to fret 5 (the target C note)
Grab the high double stop on strings 1 and 2 at fret 8
Depress the Bigsby arm slightly and release smoothly back to pitch
Execute rapid diminished sweep down from fret 10 to fret 4 over the G7 turnaround
tips: A hollowbody guitar with Filter'Tron pickups provides the essential percussive 'thunk' and top-end snap
Use analog tape slapback echo set to ~120 ms with a single repeat for authentic 1950s Sun Records depth
Keep the Bigsby motion subtle; over-bending will destabilize tuning

sections.name: Sneaking Cat Prowl Intro Riff
sections.description: The quintessential rockabilly intro. Setzer plays a walking chromatic bass line on the 5th and 6th strings, puncturing the silence with snappy staccato jazz chords.
notes: Walk into the Cm chord from the open A string: 0-1-2-3 on string 5
Chop the chord stab staccato on the upbeat
Slide into the Bb9 chord from a half-step below (A9 to Bb9)
End the 4-bar cycle on a menacing G7#9 chord with a slight Bigsby dip

sections.name: Verse Andalusian Chord Comping
sections.description: Rhythm drops into a tight, nocturnal swing groove. Setzer plays percussive comping stabs that dance effortlessly around Lee Rocker's slap-bass groove.
notes: Keep the pick-hand bounce light and bouncy at 132 BPM swing
Use fret-hand dampening to create clean percussive chops
Vary the chord voicings between the lower neck and 8th-fret barre shapes
Support the vocal narrative with tasteful dynamic restraint

sections.name: Chorus Swagger & Hook
sections.description: The title hook bursts out with infectious gang vocals and driving swing accents. Setzer digs into the lower strings for thicker, punchier rockabilly drive.
notes: Accentuate beats 2 and 4 to lock with the snare and slap-bass click
Slide aggressively into the G7 chord for maximum harmonic tension
Allow the final G7 chord to ring momentarily into the vocal breath
Feel the infectious New York street corner doo-wop swing

sections.name: Bridge Half-Diminished Detour
sections.description: The progression detours to Fm before executing a sophisticated jazz minor ii-V turnaround (Dm7b5 to G7), elevating the harmonic complexity beyond standard rock.
notes: Voice the Fm chord at fret 8 (string 5 root) or open position
Finger the Dm7b5 shape: fret 5 on string 5, fret 6 on string 4, fret 5 on string 3, fret 6 on string 2
Notice how Dm7b5 creates smooth half-step voice leading into G7
Build dynamic intensity leading straight into the iconic guitar solo

sections.name: Brian Setzer Virtuosic Solo
sections.description: Widely regarded as one of the greatest guitar solos in rockabilly history. Setzer blends blues bends, chromatic enclosures, diminished sweeps, and country-style hybrid picking with blazing swagger.
sections.progression: Cm - Bb - Ab - G7 - Fm - Cm - Dm7b5 - G7
notes: Start with the biting 8th-fret C minor pentatonic double stop
Execute the chromatic approach runs into the major 3rd of G7 (B natural)
Sweep cleanly through the Ab diminished 7th arpeggio over the G7 chord
End the phrase with a subtle, shimmering Bigsby vibrato dip

sections.name: Outro Big Band Swing Climax & Bigsby Dip
sections.description: The song ramps to its dynamic peak. Setzer trades fiery blues licks with the brass horn chart before ending on an unresolved, mysterious Cm69 chord with a slow Bigsby warble.
notes: Strum with maximum swing bravado across all six strings
Coordinate the final abrupt band stop on the upbeat of beat 4
Form the lush Cm69 chord: fret 3 on string 5, fret 1 on string 4, fret 2 on string 3, fret 3 on string 2
Dip the Bigsby arm slowly down one full step and let the natural tape echo dissolve
sections.exerciseLabel: Big Band Swing Climax & Cm69 Resolution

guitar.recommended: 1959 Gretsch 6120 'Nashville' hollowbody with TV Jones Classic / DeArmond pickups and Bigsby B6 tremolo
guitar.pickup: Bridge Filter'Tron pickup for snappy, percussive bass attack and bright rockabilly chime

amp.recommended: 1963 Fender Blonde Bassman 50W head through 2x12 cabinet with Celestion V30 speakers

effects.distortion: Natural tube preamp compression and edge-of-breakup grit
effects.other: Roland RE-301 Chorus Echo / analog tape slapback delay (approx. 120 ms, single repeat, 50% wet)

beginner.title: Mastering the Descending Minor Chords
steps: Learn basic barre chord shapes for Cm, Bb, Ab, and G7
Practice transitioning through the 4-chord Andalusian cadence in time
Strum with a metronome at 90 BPM with a swing eighth-note feel
beginner.goals: Play the foundational 4-chord descending progression with steady swing rhythm

intermediate.title: Jazz Voicings & Bass Walk-Ins
steps: Upgrade chords to Cm6, Bb9, Abmaj7, and G7#9 voicings
Incorporate the walking chromatic bass lines between chord shifts
Master the bridge minor ii-V turnaround (Dm7b5 to G7)
intermediate.goals: Perform the complete rhythm track with authentic rockabilly swing comping and clean muting

advanced.title: Brian Setzer's Virtuosic Solo
steps: Master thumb-pick hybrid picking and string-popping mechanics
Learn the chromatic enclosures, blues double stops, and diminished sweeps in the solo
Integrate expressive Bigsby vibrato dips while maintaining rock-solid pitch
advanced.goals: Perform the iconic guitar solo note-for-note with authentic vintage tone and swagger

commonMistakes: Playing with a straight rock feel instead of the essential jump-blues swing shuffle
Letting chords ring out endlessly instead of cutting them short with crisp staccato muting
Over-using the Bigsby vibrato arm, causing the hollowbody guitar to slip out of tune
Fumbling the chromatic approach notes in the solo instead of landing squarely on target chord tones
practiceRoutine: 5 mins: Chromatic walking bass exercises on strings 5 and 6 at 100 BPM swing
10 mins: Jazz chord transition practice (Cm6 - Bb9 - Abmaj7 - G7#9) with staccato chops
10 mins: Dm7b5 to G7#9 voice-leading drills in the bridge section
10 mins: Solo phrase-by-phrase transcription practice focusing on diminished arpeggio sweeps
focusAreas: Pick-hand thumb and finger independence using hybrid or thumb-pick attack
Crisp staccato release on chord chops to leave space for the upright bass
Flawless intonation on whole-step bends and chromatic enclosures
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 132 BPM in swing eighth-note mode
Practice muting strings with fret hand and executing percussive swing strums on beats 2 and 4
Gradually re-introduce the chord shapes, ensuring every downbeat lands strictly on the click
